_note: Worldwide roster proposed for scenario.1805-09 (1 September 1805). 'representation' says how each entity appears: playable (a campaign of its own); independent (on the map with its own government, run by the game, not offered as a campaign); dependent (bound to an overlord, may break away through events); associated (fights as an arm of another participant); regional-system (no single government; handled by the regional rules in README.md). 'tier' ranks playable campaigns by starting weight: major, medium, minor. Status is 'proposed' throughout; roster choices are the Owner's to approve. 'detail' marks entities with full records in nations-1805-09.json.
selection_rules: The entity existed and governed territory on the scenario date.
It could make war or peace on its own account, or its break from an overlord is a live question inside the window.
Its position gives a player decisions: neighbours worth fearing, somewhere to expand, something to protect.

Every inhabited region has at least one playable participant or a dependent with a written path to independence. South America has no independent government on this date, so it is carried by Spain's and Portugal's dependencies and gains playable participants in scenario.1810-09; that thinness is history, not omission.
Entities that differ only in name are merged or made dependent rather than listed for length.

entities.name: French Empire
entities.note: Napoleon I, Emperor since 1804 and King of Italy since 1805. The scenario's protagonist.

entities.name: Kingdom of Italy
entities.note: Viceroy Eugène de Beauharnais. Supplies troops; becomes separable only if France collapses.

entities.name: Batavian Commonwealth
entities.note: Grand Pensionary Schimmelpenninck. Holds the Cape, Java and Guiana: France's only reach into the Indian Ocean.

entities.name: Swiss Confederation
entities.note: Neutral ground and a source of capitulated regiments.

entities.name: Kingdom of Spain
entities.note: Charles IV and Godoy. France's ally, at war with Britain since December 1804. The largest overseas empire on the map and the weakest hold on it.

entities.name: Kingdom of Portugal
entities.note: Prince Regent João. Neutral, Britain's oldest ally, with Brazil larger than itself.

entities.name: United Kingdom
entities.note: George III, Pitt's second ministry. Paymaster of the coalition and master of the sea.

entities.name: East India Company
entities.note: Three presidencies with their own armies. Fights as Britain's Indian arm with its own recruitment pool and its own war with Holkar.

entities.name: Austrian Empire
entities.note: Francis, also the last Holy Roman Emperor. Joined the coalition on 9 August; Mack's army is moving on Bavaria.

entities.name: Kingdom of Prussia
entities.note: Frederick William III. Neutral, with the reputation of Frederick's army and an offer from each side.

entities.name: Russian Empire
entities.note: Alexander I. Armies marching west under Kutuzov, a second war in the Caucasus, outposts in Alaska.

entities.name: Kingdom of Sweden
entities.note: Gustav IV Adolf. In the coalition, holding Finland and Pomerania, both exposed.

entities.name: Denmark-Norway
entities.note: Crown Prince Frederick, regent. Neutral with a fleet both sides want.

entities.name: Electorate of Bavaria
entities.form: electorate of the Holy Roman Empire
entities.note: Maximilian Joseph and Montgelas. Has just chosen France; the first battlefield of the war.

entities.name: Lesser German states
entities.form: states of the Holy Roman Empire
entities.note: Württemberg, Baden, Saxony, Hesse and the rest. A bloc of small territories that align by event (Confederation of the Rhine) rather than acting singly.

entities.name: Kingdom of Naples and Sicily
entities.note: Ferdinand IV and Maria Carolina. Secretly in the coalition with a French corps on its soil; Sicily is its refuge.

entities.name: Papal States
entities.note: Pius VII. Neutral in law, under French pressure in fact; annexed in 1809 if nothing changes.

entities.name: Kingdom of Sardinia
entities.note: Reduced to the island and kept alive by British subsidy and the British fleet.

entities.name: Ottoman Empire
entities.note: Selim III. Neutral, reforming, and losing its provinces to their own governors.

entities.name: Eyalet of Egypt
entities.note: Muhammad Ali, wali since July 1805, against the Mamluk beys. Playable as a vassal that can outgrow its sultan.

entities.name: Revolutionary Serbia
entities.note: Karađorđe. In revolt since 1804 inside Ottoman territory; survival is the campaign.

entities.name: Wallachia and Moldavia
entities.note: The ground Russia and the Porte fight over from 1806.

entities.name: Regencies of Algiers, Tunis and Tripoli
entities.note: One corsair participant based on Algiers with Tunis and Tripoli as provinces. Lives by raiding trade and by tribute.

entities.name: Sultanate of Morocco
entities.note: Mawlay Sulayman. Independent of the Porte, facing Spain across the strait.

entities.name: Qajar Persia
entities.note: Fath-Ali Shah and Crown Prince Abbas Mirza. At war with Russia since 1804 and looking for a European patron.

entities.name: Emirate of Diriyah
entities.note: Saud ibn Abd al-Aziz. Holds Najd and is taking the Hejaz from the Sharif of Mecca.

entities.name: Sultanate of Muscat and Oman
entities.note: Sayyid Said. A trading and naval power from the Gulf to Zanzibar.

entities.name: Durrani Empire
entities.note: Shah Shuja. The Afghan kingdom in dynastic civil war, with Persia and the Sikhs at its edges.

entities.name: Bukhara, Khiva and Kokand
entities.note: Caravan states beyond every great power's reach in this window.

entities.name: Maratha Confederacy
entities.note: Peshwa, Scindia, Bhonsle, Holkar and Gaekwad. Beaten in 1803, with Holkar still in the field. Played as the confederacy trying to act as one.

entities.name: Sikh Empire
entities.note: Maharaja Ranjit Singh. Uniting the Punjab and building a European-drilled army.

entities.name: Kingdom of Nepal
entities.note: The Gorkha state, expanding along the Himalaya toward the Sutlej.

entities.name: Hyderabad, Awadh, Mysore and the subsidiary states
entities.note: Allied on the Company's terms; a source of troops and of revolt.

entities.name: Kingdom of Kandy
entities.note: Sri Vikrama Rajasinha. Independent in the interior of Ceylon after the war of 1803-05; a defended objective rather than a campaign. Annexed by Britain in 1815 if nothing changes.

entities.name: Qing Empire
entities.note: The Jiaqing Emperor. The largest state on earth, at peace with Europe, at war with its own rebels and pirates.

entities.name: Kingdom of Joseon
entities.note: King Sunjo's minority. Closed to the world; a tributary rather than a campaign.

entities.name: Tokugawa Shogunate
entities.note: Shogun Ienari. Secluded by policy; Rezanov's Russian embassy has just been turned away. A campaign about whether to stay closed.

entities.name: Empire of Việt Nam
entities.note: Gia Long, three years after uniting the country with French-trained officers and Vauban forts.

entities.name: Kingdom of Siam
entities.note: Rama I. Overlord of the Lao kingdoms and Cambodia, Burma's standing enemy.

entities.name: Kingdom of Burma
entities.note: Bodawpaya of the Konbaung. Expansionist toward Siam, Arakan and Assam.

entities.name: Batavian East Indies
entities.note: Java and the spice islands, cut off from Europe by the British navy.

entities.name: Malay and island sultanates
entities.note: Johor-Riau, Aceh, Brunei, Sulu: trade, piracy and local allies rather than governments to conquer.

entities.name: Captaincy General of the Philippines
entities.note: Linked to New Spain by the Manila galleon.

entities.name: United States
entities.note: President Jefferson. Neutral, doubled in size by Louisiana, with almost no army.

entities.name: British North America
entities.note: The Canadas and the Maritimes. Britain's garrison theatre against the United States.

entities.name: Viceroyalty of New Spain
entities.note: From California to Central America with Cuba and Florida attached. Breaks away through the Peninsular-crisis events.

entities.name: Viceroyalties of New Granada, Peru and Río de la Plata
entities.note: Three dependencies on the map (Bogotá, Lima, Buenos Aires) recorded under one roster line; each can become a junta.

entities.name: State of Brazil
entities.note: Becomes the seat of the monarchy if Lisbon falls.

entities.name: Empire of Haiti
entities.note: Emperor Jacques I. The only state founded by a slave revolution, surrounded by powers that want it gone.

entities.name: European sugar colonies
entities.note: Jamaica, Cuba, Martinique, Guadeloupe and the smaller islands change hands as naval objectives of their owners.

entities.name: Nations of the Plains and Southwest
entities.note: Comanche, Lakota, Apache and others. Mounted powers that control movement and trade across land no state yet governs.

entities.name: Nations of the Great Lakes and Southeast
entities.note: Shawnee, Haudenosaunee, Muscogee, Cherokee and others. Become a playable confederacy by event (Tecumseh) in later scenarios; proposed as playable from 1810-09.

entities.name: Mapuche of Araucanía
entities.note: Independent south of the Bío-Bío by treaty with Spain.

entities.name: Russian America
entities.note: Baranov's fur posts, retaken from the Tlingit in 1804.

entities.name: Sokoto jihad
entities.note: Usman dan Fodio against Gobir and the Hausa kingdoms. Starts as an army without a country.

entities.name: Gobir and the Hausa kingdoms
entities.note: Sokoto's opponents: independent kingdoms that fight the jihad one by one.

entities.name: Asante Empire
entities.note: Asantehene Osei Bonsu. Gold, muskets and a road to the coast forts, which it reaches in 1806-07.

entities.name: Dahomey, Oyo, Benin and Bornu
entities.note: Neighbours, rivals and trade partners of Asante and Sokoto.

entities.name: Ethiopian Empire
entities.form: empire in the Era of the Princes
entities.note: A powerless emperor and rival regional lords. A campaign of reunification.

entities.name: Cape Colony
entities.note: Governor Janssens. The halfway station to India; Britain's expedition is already at sea in late 1805.

entities.name: Chiefdoms of south-eastern Africa
entities.note: Mthethwa, Ndwandwe, Xhosa. The Zulu kingdom arises here after this window's midpoint.

entities.name: Kingdom of Hawaiʻi
entities.note: Kamehameha I. All islands but Kauaʻi, with foreign ships and cannon. The Pacific's only campaign: finish the unification, then choose a patron or none.

entities.name: New South Wales
entities.note: A British naval station and little more.

entities.name: Peoples of Oceania
entities.note: Māori iwi, Tahiti under Pōmare II, Tonga, Aboriginal nations. Present as places with their own defenders, trade and consequences, not as conquest targets with governments.
